interpretation.reproduced: The first three observations (2026-11-17, and twice on 2026-11-20) agreed 5/5 on the observed redirect targets. The fourth observation (2026-11-20, session b0920c92) does not: four of the five submitted short links ended on the Amazon home page, and only B0f3GKalj still resolved to a product listing. The earlier agreement is therefore not a guarantee that those short links resolve to those products today.
interpretation.what_reproduction_does_not_prove: Every final URL ever observed carries lv=shuf (shuffle) and plpRedirect=mhFallback (listing-page fallback). That is a fallback route, not a canonical resolution of the submitted token, which is why the intended_* fields stay blank. The fourth observation adds a second reason to keep them blank: the submitted short links did not all resolve to product pages on the most recent pass. Nothing here says the short links are invalid — FLG-003 remains open and unresolved.
interpretation.operational_consequence: The reader-facing links on this site are NOT the submitted short links. They are built from the observed ASINs as direct https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> URLs. All five of those were re-opened directly on 2026-11-20 as a control and every one still served the product page and breadcrumb recorded in data/products.json. So the published links are unaffected by the short-link behaviour; what needs the owner's attention is confirming the intended destination for each product (Q-02) and the one-link Associates test (FLG-002). The short links' behaviour is published as FLG-026 rather than resolved here.
